# Casberi — Full documentation

> Keep it moving, privately. Your life and money are spread across accounts; you spend the day switching between apps to get anything done. Casberi is a wallet that keeps it all moving, privately: connect your apps and everything lands in one private feed on your device, beside one balance for every account you have and follow. Free on iPhone and iPad, with no Casberi account, ever.

Website: https://casberi.app · Docs: https://casberi.app/docs.html · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/casberi/id6788637831 · Privacy: https://casberi.app/privacy.html

Last updated: November 16, 2026 · Describes Casberi 3.0.40. The App Store may be a version behind.

## What Casberi does

Three things: read everything your apps bring in, see and move your money, and keep it yours.

### Read

- Activity — What happened, in your money and in every app you connect: one row per app, under what needs you.
- Apps — Connect mail, photos, wallets, calendars and a hundred more apps.
- Search — Share from any app or take a screenshot, then find it by what it says.

### Money

- Home — Every account you have and follow in one balance, with holdings, spending and risks. Following is read-only.
- Your account — A public account (Safe) on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood, a private balance (Privacy Pools and Railgun) on Ethereum, and a private account (Aztec) on Aztec. Only your keys move them.
- Move — Buy, earn, receive, send and swap, in public or privately. You hold to approve, and Face ID signs.

### Yours

- Subscriptions — What renews and when, found on its own. What it costs, in Spending.
- Privacy — No sign-up, no server, no analytics. Every wallet read goes through Tor on iPhone and iPad.
- Your options — The order of Activity, widgets, theme, notifications, and where your data lives.

## How to use — the whole app

Four steps to start. Then one short page for each part of the app.

### Start here

1. Open it. There's no account and nothing to sign up for. The first time, Set up your wallet makes your account, and Set up your feed offers six apps to start with.
2. Tap Apps, under your balance on Home. It holds every app you can connect, by category.
3. Pick one and connect it. Calendar and Photos are one tap; an account needs only an address.
4. Scroll down Home. What you connected is there.

Casberi is one page. Home starts with your money: your balance, Public by network and Private by place, then Account, Risks and Apps. Under it is what's new: Needs you, Activity, and a section for each kind of app. Move, the circle at the bottom, is what you do with your money, and the only thing on the bar. A page's title says where you are: its grey words go back, and so does a swipe to the right. On iPad, Home is cards and Activity is a place of its own.

### Home

Home adds up every account you have and follow, so you see all your money in one place, and what could hurt it.

- See what you have. Home leads with your balance and its day. Under it, Public is a row per network and Private a row per place: Privacy Pools, Railgun and Aztec. Tap the balance for Holdings, which is Public and Private: your tokens, positions and NFTs, then everything private — Privacy Pools, Railgun and Aztec — in one block.
- Choose whose money. Yours · Following · All, at the top of Holdings, shows your own account, the accounts you follow, or everything added up. Home follows it.
- See what you spend. Spending, a row under Activity, sets this week or month against the last one, split into Subscriptions, Places, Fees and Round-ups. Fees and round-ups stay out of the total.
- See what could hurt you. Risks, under your balance, counts what's new. It lists address poisoning, fake tokens and fake transfers, what a privacy scan of your account found, and who can spend from you: each approval one tap from a cancellation, and what you've let apps on Aztec do, each with Take back. Mark all as seen puts what you've read away, and Seen brings it back. Under Approvals, your co-signer's keys open on Revoke.cash.
- Watch a token. Watchlist follows the price of any token, whether you hold it or not. Its line leads Activity on Home.
- Follow an account. Following, on Account, takes an address, ENS, .sol or basename, or a wallet app or an exchange.

Good to know: following is read-only. It asks for no permissions, so it can never trade or move funds.

If you use DeFi: home also carries Aave and Morpho health, Uniswap positions in or out of range, Hyperliquid liquidation distance, Aerodrome locks and their weekly vote deadline, staked ETH and HYPE, exchange balances and validators — all in one total.

A Safe reads as a Safe: owners, threshold, signature queue. If this device is an owner, Sign sends that one signature to Safe's own service after Face ID; it can never execute a transaction on its own. MetaMask Card, ether.fi and Plasma One card spends, Peer onramp fills, 0xBow deposits clearing and Railgun shields show as ordinary rows. Spam folds into a pile you can mute.

### Activity

Activity is what happened, in your money and in every app you connect, so you don't open ten apps to see.

On iPhone it's the lower half of Home. A row of your apps' icons comes first; each jumps to its section. Then Needs you, when something waits on you, in your account or your apps. Then Activity: your watchlist, Spending and your latest move. Then a section for each kind of app — Day, Notes, Social, Work, Media, Life and Agents — with one row per app: its icon and its newest thing. A post or a chat shows the person's face. Before you add an app, Activity shows your six latest moves.

Day is each app's next thing: meetings, reminders and renewals. Activity opens every move, by day.

Tap any row to open it, then open it in the app it came from, or share it. Some rows let you act in place: start an email, put an event on your calendar, turn a note into a reminder. Each write asks first.

### Your account

An account of your own lets you move money from Casberi, with no phrase to write down. Casberi never holds it: only your keys can move it. It lives on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood.

It comes in three parts: your public account (a Safe, on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood), your private balance (Privacy Pools and Railgun, on Ethereum) and your private account (Aztec, on Aztec). See Private money. The private account is made the first time you use it, from a key in your iCloud Keychain, and every transaction it makes is proved on your iPhone.

Your account is made for you the first time you open Casberi. Finish setup, on Home, takes four steps:

1. A recovery key in iCloud Keychain. If you lose this device, your account opens on another.
2. A co-signer in another wallet, if you want one. That wallet signs once to prove it can.
3. Require your co-signer, if you added one. Every send and swap then needs it too.
4. Round-ups, if you want them. See Move.

- See your account. Account, the first word under your balance, opens on your public account: its address, its networks and Copy. Tap your face or name to set them. Under it, Private account opens your Aztec account, and Following is the accounts you follow. Then your keys: this iPhone, Backup, the co-signer and Export keys. Then Networks, Tor and Nodes, round-ups and your savings goal, and last, Casberi's settings.
- See your Aztec address. Private account opens a page of its own: your Aztec address, one tap to copy. It's paid from Aztec only, and pays out to Aztec or Ethereum. The address at the top of Account is always your public one.
- Check your recovery key. Once a month, Needs you asks you to: Face ID and a test signature, no fee, nothing sent.
- Take it elsewhere. Export keys asks which account. For your Safe it makes a new private key, adds it as an owner on every network, Robinhood included, and shows it once, so the account opens in another wallet without Casberi. For Aztec it shows the account's own keys once. Your co-signer approves either.
- Use your own node. Nodes reads your account from a node you run, Aztec included, each address checked against its network first.

Good to know: when you require your co-signer, getting your account back on a new device needs your co-signer too, and its wallet shows a code to approve that Casberi shows you to match. The co-signer is a second look at every send and swap, not a lock against this device: this device holds its own key and your recovery key, so it can turn the co-signer off with Face ID. See Security.

### Move

Move is where you do something with your money. Tap Move and five verbs rise over the page: Buy, Earn, Receive, Send and Swap. Each is one page with a line for each thing it asks, its answer in a chip. Tap a chip to choose; for a person or a token, type in it to search. The amount goes on Casberi's own keys. When it's ready, the page reads as a receipt: hold the act, Hold to send or Hold to swap, and Face ID signs.

#### Pay someone

- Send money. Pick who it's to, the token and the amount; a token comes with its network. To lists yours first — Privacy Pools, Railgun and Aztec — then the addresses you paid last and your contacts, and takes a name, an ENS name or a pasted address. An address that looks like one of your contacts says so, in amber. Add another puts a second send or swap in the same transaction.
- Pay a name. Type a zk.money tag, or @name, in To and Send sets the payment up. Any token on Ethereum is swapped into USDC in the same transaction; from another network, Across carries the dollar there. Each payment goes to a fresh address. From your private balance, a tag is paid in USDC. Save a tag and it's a contact with Pay.
- Pay a contact. A contact with a wallet has Send on their page in Contacts. Move opens with their name filled in.

#### Get money in

- Receive. To your public account takes any token on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood. From another network takes USDC or that network's own token from most other networks. Under Private, To Privacy Pools, To Railgun and To Aztec each say what they take and who can pay them. Tap a row's Copy for its address (see Private money).
- Buy. Buy is tokens or gift cards. Tokens are paid by card on Stripe's own page, never by Casberi, and arrive in your account. A gift card comes from Bitrefill, paid from your account, and its code shows once it's bought.

#### Change what you hold

- Swap. Your phone asks Uniswap and Aerodrome directly for the best price and writes the swap itself, with no aggregator in between. Move names the exchange and its pool fee, which is in the price.
- Swap later. When sets a price; the order waits on CoW Swap and fills when the price is reached.
- Swap to another network. Pick a token on another network as what you get, and Across carries it: ETH arrives as ETH, USDC as USDC. Activity shows it arriving.
- Clear out dust. Sweep, in Swap, swaps every token worth under $1, or $5, on one network for ETH, in one transaction. A token it won't touch stays listed with the reason — most dust is sent by strangers.

#### Spend it, or put it to work

- Earn. Earn puts a token of yours on Aave, where it earns; Withdraw takes it back. What's lent has its own rows in Holdings.
- Round up. Every buy, send and swap rounds up to the next $1 or $5, your pick. The change is set aside on Aave on Base, where it earns, and once it reaches $10 the next send moves it into your private balance. What it saved is in Spending, under Round-ups.

#### Keep it private

- Go private. In Send, pick Privacy Pools, Railgun or Aztec in To. To pay privately, pick a token under one of them. See Private money.

#### Before you approve

- The fee. When it's ready, the receipt's Fee says the most it can be.
- Pay the fee without ETH. On Base, a send short of ETH for its fee pays it from your USDC, up to $5 at a time. Face ID asks once to allow that, then once for the send.
- What you sign. The receipt says whether this exact move was run on the network first and lands as written. Details holds what it was checked against and the transaction itself, which is what Face ID signs.
- A warning. It stands on the receipt: the move would fail, the address is sanctioned or reported, it looks like an address you've paid, it's a new contract, or it's your first send there. Read it before you hold.
- Over what you have. The amount turns amber and says how much more you need.
- Your co-signer. When you require it, every send and swap needs it too.

### Private money

Two private places. Your private balance is on Ethereum, and you never choose where it sits: Casberi picks Privacy Pools or Railgun by the token. Your private account is on Aztec, an account of its own. Both show under Private in Holdings.

- Add money. Tap Add money under Private in Holdings, or in Send, pick Privacy Pools, Railgun or Aztec in To. Privacy Pools and Railgun take $10 at least; Aztec, any amount you type.
- Pay someone privately. In Send, pick a token under Privacy Pools, Railgun or Aztec. Your public account appears nowhere on the payment. A zk.money tag can be paid from your private balance too.
- Swap privately. In Swap, pick a token under Railgun: it swaps for another Railgun token without leaving Railgun.
- Send to someone's Railgun. Paste their 0zk address in To. It stays inside Railgun, with a note only they can read.
- Base and Robinhood. ETH and dollars sent to your private balance on Base or Robinhood move to Ethereum to earn, and your private balance can pay an address there; Across carries it.
- Get paid privately. In Receive, To Privacy Pools gives each payment a fresh address of its own, for ETH, USDC and USDG. To Railgun is your 0zk address, paid from Railgun. To Aztec is your Aztec address, paid from Aztec.
- See it, and take it back. Holdings is Public by network and Private by place, each heading the same figure Home shows. Under Railgun, a row reads "DAI 400 — Ethereum"; one that isn't spendable yet says "Private in about an hour". Tap a row to open its token.
- Use private apps. An Aztec app's link opens in Casberi and uses your private account; apps you connect stand in Apps.
- Tacit. Add Tacit in Apps and tap Connect: your co-signer opens the Tacit account you already have, and Casberi reads it. Its page is Public and Private: TAC in your wallet; private TAC on the Tacit chain and in Tacit's DeFi pool; private ETH on Ethereum and Robinhood; and what your Tacit chain shares have earned from its fees. Make private moves public TAC to the Tacit chain: Casberi proves the deposit on your iPhone, your co-signer signs one permit for exactly the amount and Tacit's fee, and it lands in about a minute; one the chain doesn't take goes back to your DeFi pool. Buy TAC opens Swap. Receive names each address: Tacit chain for private TAC, Private for private ETH from another Tacit account, Deposit for ETH from an exchange, Public for your wallet. Nothing moves without your co-signer's signature.

Where it sits, and who carries it:

| | Holding | Sending | Receiving |
|---|---|---|---|
| Privacy Pools | ETH and USDC. Earns on Aave. $10 at least. | From Privacy Pools to anyone on Ethereum. | Someone on Ethereum sends you ETH or USDC: it lands in Privacy Pools. |
| Railgun | Any other token on Ethereum. $10 at least. | From Railgun to anyone on Ethereum. | Someone on Ethereum sends you DAI, USDT, WBTC, WETH, LINK, UNI or AAVE: it lands in Railgun. |
| Your Aztec account | ETH and USDC. Its own account on Aztec, filled through Shield. | From your Aztec account to anyone on Ethereum or anyone on Aztec. | Someone on Aztec sends you ETH or USDC: it lands in your Aztec account. |

All three show together under Private in Holdings. You send from whichever one holds the money. Who sends to you, and with what, decides where it lands.

- Into your private balance. ETH and USDC go into 0xBow's Privacy Pools, which approves each deposit before it can be spent, and once approved it earns on Aave. Any other token goes into Railgun and is private in about an hour; Railgun takes 0.25% in and 0.25% out. Move names which one.
- Into your private account. USDC or ETH moves into your Aztec account through Shield. Up to $100 a day, this iPhone signs it with a key made only for Shield; past that, your co-signer signs, with a Human Passport score of 20. The first time, 30 AZTEC goes along as private gas.
- Who posts a payment. From Privacy Pools, 0xBow's relayer. From Railgun, a Railgun broadcaster, which takes its fee inside Railgun, shown before Face ID; if none answers, a fresh address of yours posts it, its gas paid from your private ETH. From your Aztec account, a payment to an Aztec address stays private on Aztec; to an Ethereum address it leaves through Shield, signed by your co-signer, and Needs you offers Finish about an hour later.
- What arrives at a fresh address. It moves in by the table above, its gas paid from your private ETH.

Round-ups, if you turn them on: every buy, send and swap rounds up to the next $1 or $5; the change earns on Aave on Base, in the open; at $10, it goes private into Privacy Pools, still earning.

Good to know: what goes in and what comes out is public on its network, as on every network; what stays hidden is which deposit paid which payment. See Privacy and Security.

### Apps

Apps is where you connect apps and find everything that's yours. It's under your balance on Home.

It's a search field and folders, one for each category with its apps. Tap an app you have and its page opens; hold it for Open and Settings. Two open a page of their own: Contacts, in Social, and Calendar, in Day, which is your calendars and the ones you subscribe to. In the Wallet folder, the Aztec apps you've connected stand as tiles, and connect again on their own.

Contacts is everyone you deal with, one row a person: the cards on your phone, the people you follow and the names in your wallet. A contact with a wallet has Send, and one with a zk.money tag has Pay. When a transfer names an address you don't know, Save asks who it is: someone you have, or a new name. Every transfer with them then reads the name.

Over a hundred apps, connecting three ways:

- One tap for the Apple apps you already use — Photos, Calendar, Reminders, Health, Music, Contacts, Apple Wallet.
- A sign-in or a pasted token for services — Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, and more.
- Nothing at all for accounts. Type an address.

### Subscriptions

Casberi finds what you pay for again and again, so nothing renews without you seeing it.

Every subscription is in Apps, under Subscriptions, with the day it renews. Casberi finds a charge that repeats at one price, from your cards, Apple Wallet or Rocket Money. Add any it missed with Track a subscription. What they cost is in Spending, under Subscriptions, with the month's total and a calendar of renewals.

The mailing lists that write to you are under Mail lists, each with a way out. To follow a calendar you don't own, paste its link — webcal:// or an .ics — under Calendars. Its events land in Day.

### Notes

Notes keeps everything you write in one place: your own notes, and what Obsidian, Notion, Day One and Apple Journal hold.

It's a section of Activity; your notes' page — All, Folders, Voice — is in Apps' Notes folder. Check off a list, record a voice note, attach a picture or a sketch, file into folders, or lock one. A passage you keep from anything you read lands here as a highlight.

### Search

Anything you save, you can find again by what it says.

Type in Apps' field. Apps, accounts, people, notes, subscriptions and your things show under their categories, and a tap goes there. Find, the last row, searches your things by what they say. Spotlight finds them too.

To save something, share it from any app. Screenshots come in on their own and are searchable by what's in them; voice notes are transcribed. Save to Casberi in Control Center opens the composer from anywhere — paste to save, or tap the mic and talk. Typing alone never saves. Casberi note starts a note.

Four widgets put Casberi on your Home Screen: Notes shows your two newest notes, Wallet your balance, its day, and Public and Private, Feed each app's newest thing today, and Watchlist your first four tokens and their day.

### Privacy

Casberi has no server and no analytics. Your things are kept in a database on your device, and what leaves it goes straight from your device to the service it's for — never through Casberi, because there is nowhere for it to pass.

- Your things. On your device. iCloud sync is off until you turn it on; on, they're in your own iCloud, encrypted in transit and on Apple's servers, with Apple holding the keys unless you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
- Your apps. Each one is read from your device, from its own service, under that service's own privacy policy. A key you paste goes only to the service it's for.
- Your wallets. On iPhone and iPad, every request that names a wallet — yours or one you follow — goes through Tor, always, with one route per wallet, so no service learns where you are, or that the wallets you look at are one person's. The Feed's apps never go through Tor.
- Your moves. Sends, swaps and sweeps go through Tor too. What lands on a network is public there, as on every network: the addresses, the amounts and the time.
- Your private balance. Money going into it and coming out of it is public on Ethereum; what stays hidden is which deposit paid which payment. 0xBow approves each deposit before it can be spent privately, and its relayer sends what you pay out, so it sees where the money goes and how much, never who asked. Receiving to your private balance on Ethereum gives each payment its own fresh address.
- Your Railgun balance. The same is true of Railgun: going in and coming out are public on Ethereum, and what stays hidden is which deposit paid which payment. A payment to someone else is posted by a Railgun broadcaster, reached over Tor on iPhone and iPad, so neither it nor Ethereum sees your account; if no broadcaster answers, a fresh address of yours posts it instead, its gas paid from your private ETH. Railgun's screening lists each deposit before it can be spent, about an hour.
- Your private account. On Aztec, everything is private by default: your balance, who you pay, how much, and the apps you use. Your iPhone makes the proof for every transaction itself, so what you do never leaves it unencrypted. Casberi reads Aztec through Tor from a public node, or from your own. Shield, the bridge in and out, sees the address that signs and the amount when you move money, and asks for a Human Passport score past $100 a day in, and to move money out; an Aztec app you open in Casberi sees your Aztec address only once you connect it.
- What your screenshots say. Read by Apple's Vision on your device, and named by Apple's on-device model. A screenshot that shows a password, a recovery phrase, a key, a card number or a code keeps those lines out of Spotlight and out of anything sent to an agent.
- Agents. Nothing goes to a model unless you connect an agent and send to it; then it goes from your device straight to that provider, billed to you. Apple Intelligence answers on Apple's Private Cloud Compute.
- Copying. What you copy expires after ten minutes. An address, a code or a key you copy stays on this device and expires after two.
- Notifications. Made on your device. There's no server to send them.

Good to know: a few services refuse Tor and are read directly — among them Relay, so Receive from another network, and a round-up bought on another network, say "not through Tor".

What this app reaches, in Casberi's settings under Data, lists every service Casberi can reach and what it actually reached, including how much went through Tor and which services refuse it.

### Security

Casberi holds none of your keys, and runs no server that could. Every key is made on your device and kept in its Secure Enclave or its Keychain. The ones that must survive a lost device sync through iCloud Keychain, which is end-to-end encrypted, so your Apple account is what protects them.

- This device's key. Made in the Secure Enclave, it never leaves it and signs only after Face ID. Every send moves your account to a fresh one. Re-enrolling Face ID destroys it; your recovery key brings your account back.
- Your recovery key. In iCloud Keychain, so every device signed in to your Apple account holds it. It never signs a payment: it only moves your account to a new device, after Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode. Once a month, Needs you asks you to check it.
- Your co-signer, if you add one: a key in another wallet you hold. Required, it approves every send and swap too, and every transaction from your private account on Aztec. Your Safe enforces it on its networks; on Aztec, Casberi does.
- Your private balance's key. One secret in iCloud Keychain, with your Railgun wallet's key beside it. The keys that spend your private balance are worked out from it on your device when they're needed and kept only in memory, and spending asks for Face ID first.
- Your private account's key. One secret in iCloud Keychain, readable only by Casberi. The keys that sign and read your Aztec account are worked out from it on your device and kept only in memory, and every transaction asks for Face ID. A new iPhone signed in to your Apple account gets your Aztec account back.
- Your Tacit key. Opening Tacit asks your co-signer to sign Tacit's own message, the one every Tacit app asks for, and that signature is your Tacit key: whoever holds it controls your Tacit money. Casberi asks only when you tap Connect or Open, checks the signature came from your co-signer, and never asks for any other message. The key is rebuilt from it each time and kept only in memory while Tacit is open; closing Tacit or the app drops it. What Casberi found on the Tacit chain is kept in the Keychain on this device only, never synced: it shows what you hold and can't spend it, and removing Tacit deletes it.
- An exported key. Export makes a new private key for your Safe, adds it as an owner and shows it once; Casberi keeps only its address. For Aztec, it shows the account's own keys once.
- Your apps' keys. A key you paste syncs through iCloud Keychain to your other devices. Sign-ins and tokens that refresh stay on this device and out of backups. Delete access removes them all.
- A locked note's key is in iCloud Keychain, so the note opens on your other devices.
- Keys that sign for others. When Casberi co-signs a Safe you share, its key stays on this device behind Face ID and can't move money on its own. Testnet keys stay on this device and sign on testnets only.

Who can move your money. This device, after Face ID. Whoever holds your Apple account and the passcode of one of your devices holds your recovery key, your private balance's key and your private account's key: without a co-signer, that's enough to move your account to another device, and the two private keys spend on their own. With your co-signer required, moving your account to another device needs your co-signer too, and Casberi asks it before any Aztec transaction; a copy of Casberi someone has altered could skip that, which is why your Apple account and your passcode are what protect your private money.

Good to know: the co-signer is a second look at every send and swap, not a lock against this device. This device holds its own key and your recovery key, so anyone who can unlock it can turn the co-signer off and then send. Keep a passcode on your devices; iCloud Keychain already needs two-factor sign-in on your Apple account.

### Your options

Casberi's own settings close the Account page: your data, the order of Activity's sections, theme, notifications, language, support and licenses.

Your data is all on your device. Export, import or delete it anytime, and turn iCloud sync on if you want it.

Notifications are two switches, Wallet and Feed. They arrive as Casberi finds them, one per app.

An agent you bring — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Venice, Bankr, OpenRouter, Grok, NEAR AI or Muse — connects from Apps like every other app. Its key lives in the Keychain, and what it sends goes from your device straight to that provider, billed to you. Your own model is a server you run that speaks OpenAI's format: give its address, a key only if it asks for one, and pick a model. Apple Intelligence needs no key. In the composer, the agent you connected is picked; Send asks it, and if it fails, it says so. There is no Casberi server in between.

### If something's missing

- I connected an app and nothing showed up — Pull down on Home to refresh. If it's an Apple app, check iOS Settings → Casberi and make sure you said yes. Some apps are quiet on purpose: Trello, for instance, only shows cards assigned to you, and the app tells you so.
- My screenshots aren't updating — Photos needs full access, not selected photos: iOS Settings → Casberi → Photos → All Photos. That's also what lets a screenshot you delete in Photos disappear here.
- An account shows no balance — Give the first read a moment, then pull to refresh. Pick Following at the top of Holdings and check the address.
- Tor can't connect, or my wallets aren't refreshing — Account shows Tor as On, Connecting or Can't connect. Some networks block Tor: try another Wi-Fi, or cellular. Casberi starts Tor's connections again when your network changes. Until it connects, each wallet shows its last reading, with its time.
- A swap was refused before Face ID — Before you sign, the network runs this exact swap. If it would pay less than the least you accept — the price moved since the quote — or would fail, Casberi won't sign it, and Move says why. Nothing was sent or paid. Try again for a fresh price, or a smaller amount.
- A swap to another network is still on its way — Activity shows it arriving until a relayer fills it on the other network. If none fills it in time, Across's contract refunds it on the network it left. ETH comes back as WETH, which Swap turns back into ETH one for one.
- A subscription is missing — Casberi counts a charge once it has repeated at the same price, about a month apart. Connect the card or Apple Wallet it's paid from, or add it yourself with Track a subscription in Apps.


## Every app

Over a hundred apps, in nine catalog categories: Wallet, Testnets, Work, Agents, Day, Notes, Life, Social and Media. The full list, each with one line, is on https://casberi.app/docs.html#every-app.

## Questions, answered

- Do I need an account? — No. There's nothing to sign up for — Casberi works the moment it's installed.
- Where do my things live? — In a database on your device. No Casberi server holds them, and iCloud sync stays off until you turn it on. Deleting is two clear choices: Delete things wipes your data (this device and iCloud), Delete access removes every token and key Casberi holds.
- What does it cost? — It's free on the App Store.
- What do I need to run it? — An iPhone or iPad. Nothing is billed, and no question goes to a model unless you connect an agent and send to it — then it goes straight to that provider, or to your own server. Connected apps do reach their own services to fetch your things; that traffic goes from your device to them, never through a Casberi server.
- Does Casberi hold my money? — No. Your account is a Safe that only your keys can move: this device's key, a recovery key in your iCloud Keychain, and a co-signer in another wallet if you add one. Export a private key and the account opens in another wallet without Casberi.
- Is there a seed phrase? — No. This device's key lives in its Secure Enclave, never leaves it and signs only with Face ID, and each send moves your account to a fresh one. Your recovery key is in your iCloud Keychain. Casberi can also co-sign a Safe you share with others: it adds a signature and can never move money on its own.
- Can it act without asking? — No. Typed text never saves silently, and any write that leaves the app waits for a tap. Following an account is read-only — it can never trade or move funds. Your account moves money only when you hold the act in Move and Face ID signs; if you require your co-signer, it approves every send and swap too, and a round-up buys only inside a move you approved. A Safe signature leaves only when you tap Sign and pass Face ID, and can never execute a transaction on its own. Bankr is only ever asked questions, never given instructions.
- What if I lose my phone? — Your account's recovery key is in your iCloud Keychain, so the account opens on a new device signed in to the same Apple account. If you require your co-signer, getting it back needs it too: its wallet shows a code to approve, and Casberi shows the same code to match. Your things come back only if you turned iCloud sync on; apps you connected can be connected again.
- What does a swap cost? — The network's fee, and the exchange pool's fee, which is in the price. A swap to another network adds Across's fee, and a private swap inside Railgun pays Railgun 0.5% and its broadcaster. Casberi takes nothing. Move shows each before Face ID.
- Is it audited? — Casberi's own code has not been independently audited. It deploys no contract of its own: your account is built from Safe's audited contracts and, when you require your co-signer, Rhinestone's audited OwnableValidator, and swaps call Uniswap, Aerodrome and Across contracts directly. Every move is run on the network before Face ID, and the source is public under the GPLv3.
- How do round-ups work? — Turn on round-ups and every buy, send and swap rounds up to the next $1 or $5, your pick. The change is set aside on Aave on Base, where it earns in the open. Once it reaches $10, the next send moves it into your private balance in Privacy Pools, where it keeps earning: one Face ID for both. What it saved is under Spending, in Round-ups, and stays out of your spending total.
- How does my private balance work? — It's money only you can see, on Ethereum. You never choose where it sits: ETH and USDC go into 0xBow's Privacy Pools, where 0xBow reviews each deposit before it can be spent and it earns interest on Aave once approved; any other token goes into Railgun, private in about an hour. Tap Add money under Private in Holdings, or in Send pick Privacy Pools or Railgun in To, $10 at least. To pay from it, pick a private token in Send's token list: a relayer or a Railgun broadcaster posts the payment for a fee shown before Face ID, so it doesn't come from your account's address. Take it back returns it to your account at any time. Your account owns it; Casberi never does.
- How does my private account on Aztec work? — It's an account of its own on Aztec, where your balance, payments and apps are all private. It's made the first time you use it, from a key in your iCloud Keychain, and every transaction is proved on your iPhone. In Send, pick Aztec in To to move USDC or ETH in through Shield, any amount you type. Up to $100 a day, this iPhone signs it; past that, your co-signer signs, with a Human Passport score of 20. The first time, 30 AZTEC goes along as gas. To pay from it, pick its token under Private in Send's token list: privately to any Aztec account, or out to any Ethereum address. An Aztec app's link opens in Casberi, and the app connects once you pick Casberi in it and match the emoji. An app you've connected stands in Apps' Wallet folder as a tile, and what you've let it do is in Risks, with Take back.
- What if Casberi goes away? — Your money stays where it is. Export a private key from Account: it's added as an owner of your account and shown once, and the account opens in another wallet without Casberi.
- Which networks? — Your account is on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood Chain. The accounts you follow are read on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, HyperEVM, Monad, World Chain, Arc, Tempo, Plasma, Robinhood Chain and Solana, plus Bitcoin wallets and the exchanges you connect.
- Why Tor? — So no service you ask about a wallet learns where you are, or that the wallets you look at belong to one person. It's always on for wallet reads on iPhone and iPad, and your other apps never go through it.


## How it's built

The source is public under the GPLv3. Every claim on this page has a file behind it.

- No server. Every request goes from your device straight to the service it names. Every host it can reach (https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/hosts.md), listed from the code.
- Your keys stay yours. Where each key lives, what it can sign, and what unlocks it. Architecture and threat model (https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md).
- Check it yourself. One command per claim, with the output to expect. Verify it yourself (https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/verify-it-yourself.md).
- What it runs on. Every dependency, with its version, source and licence. Dependencies (https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/dependencies.md).
- Not audited yet. Casberi's own code has had no independent audit. The threat model says what to read first.
- Found a problem? Report it privately. Security policy (https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
